title: Ricursive Intelligence is betting on AI-designed chips to help solve the compute crisis
key_facts: Founders Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini spoke at TechCrunch Disrupt on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026.
Their startup Ricursive Intelligence builds AI that designs chips, learns from each design and improves the next.
Goldie said demand for compute could be at least 10,000 times higher in five years and she would rather make chips more efficient than build 10,000 times more data centres.
Their earlier AlphaChip system produced an unexpected "donut-shaped" layout that proved successful.
They optimise whole chips rather than splitting them into dozens of blocks.
Goldie said designing a chip in about a week could make custom chips for many uses worthwhile.
quote_evidence: “There is this understanding that in the next five years we are going to have at least 10,000x more demand for compute, and that’s somewhat potentially conservative,” Goldie said on stage.
The founders say AI is challenging traditional chip design methods by discovering unconventional layouts that can outperform traditional ones.
why_it_matters_hint: Faster, AI-driven chip design is pitched as a way to ease compute demand without building vastly more data centres.
notes: Founders' own claims at a conference; no independent test reported.
